Restore the class of a tibble from its genotypes column

Source: R/genotypes_tbl_class.R
genotypes_tbl_class.Rd

Some dplyr operations return tibbles that have lost the class of a gen_tibble, such as the data frames returned by pick() or across() within summarise(), reframe() or mutate(), the result of reframe(), or as_tibble(). Their genotypes column, however, keeps its class. The generics of tidypopgen therefore have fallback methods for data frames (and grouped data frames), which use restore_genotypes_tbl() to give back the tibble its class, as given by genotypes_tbl_class() for its genotypes column, and then dispatch again.

Usage

genotypes_tbl_class(genotypes, ...)

# Default S3 method
genotypes_tbl_class(genotypes, ...)

# S3 method for class 'vctrs_bigSNP'
genotypes_tbl_class(genotypes, ...)

restore_genotypes_tbl(.x, generic = "this function")

Arguments

genotypes

the genotypes column of a tibble

...

currently unused

.x

a data frame or tibble with a genotypes column

generic

the name of the generic for which the class is restored, used in the error message if the restored class has no method

Value

genotypes_tbl_class() returns the class of the tibble that holds the genotypes column ("gen_tbl" for a vctrs_bigSNP column), or NULL for a column of an unknown class.

restore_genotypes_tbl() returns .x as a tibble with the class given by genotypes_tbl_class(), and its grouped version (e.g. "grouped_gen_tbl") if .x is grouped. A rowwise_df is ungrouped. It stops with an error if .x already has that class, as the generic would otherwise dispatch to the fallback method again.

Details

Packages that build their own tibbles on tidypopgen (e.g. the gl_tibble of tidypopgl) add a method to genotypes_tbl_class() for the class of their genotypes column, so that their own methods of the tidypopgen generics are used after the class is restored.
